rationale:
ROUND 1 WAS RIGHT AND THE OBJECTION WAS SUBSTANTIVE, NOT STYLISTIC. The reuse_agent seat gated on the exclusion hand-rolling `p.deployed_at IS NULL` instead of calling datahelpers.NeverDeployedPagePredicateFor. I checked, and the seat was right twice over: the builder exists (platform/orchestration/datahelpers/links.go:277), roughly fourteen sibling checks in this very package already call the shared family, and — the part that matters — THE BUILDER IS NOT WHAT I WROTE. It is `deployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(build_status, <empty>) <> 'deployed'`. The second conjunct exists specifically to spare a page marked deployed but never stamped, and per that helper's own doc such a page SERVES 200. My hand-rolled half would have excluded it.

So round 1 shipped a latent defect, and I am stating its size honestly rather than inflating it to flatter the reviewer: measured 2026-08-15, both spellings select the SAME 1 page today, and the divergence class (archived AND deployed_at IS NULL AND build_status = 'deployed') is currently ZERO rows. The one row of that shape fleet-wide is idea.uk/tools.html#audience-check, which is status='active'. The defect would have bitten the moment that row was archived, not before.

The original problem is unchanged: a rejected draft archived without ever being published is re-scanned on every daily sweep, files findings, and cannot close (webdesign.uk/index-rejected-v1-20260806, 19 banned-claim findings, item a355d78b). The predicate is still the conjunction archived AND never-deployed, still because five archived pages were measured serving HTTP 200. What changed is that its never-deployed half now comes from the estate's one definition instead of my retyping of it.

plan.summary: Round 2. Same exclusion, but the never-deployed half is now datahelpers.NeverDeployedPagePredicateFor("p") rather than hand-written SQL. Adds a doc note saying why this check deliberately does NOT adopt PageHasShippedPredicateFor like its ~14 siblings. Corrects a stale call-site citation the prior_art_librarian seat challenged. The contract test now derives its expectation from the builder instead of a literal, and grew an arm that fails if the half is re-typed by hand — so the round 1 defect is regression-locked. Also fixes a gofmt violation the round 1 code shipped with. NOTE ON EDIT COUNT: this plan lists only the TWO edits that change executed behaviour. Three further changes in the same commits are comment-only — the why-not-PageHasShippedPredicateFor note, the corrected stale call-site citation, and a gofmt fix — and are described in grounded_in rather than listed as edits, per editquality's round 1 point that disclosure should not be counted as substantive coverage.

COMMENT-ONLY CHANGE, not listed as an edit (doc comment — stale call-site citation, corrected in place): ANSWERS prior_art_librarian objection 1 (MEDIUM). My round 1 comment cited `status='active' AND build_status='deployed'` as live at 'load_site_pages_action.go:80 and four sibling call sites', carried verbatim from a LANDMINES.md entry. COMMENT-ONLY CHANGE, not listed as an edit (gofmt compliance of the doc comment): Round 1 shipped this file not gofmt-clean and the build gate rejects that. Cause worth recording: since Go 1.19 gofmt reformats DOC COMMENTS and still honours the legacy TeX-style quoting convention, so a doubled apostrophe becomes a Unicode close quote. SQL's empty-string literal IS a doubled apostrophe, so quoting the predicate verbatim in a comment makes gofmt silently corrupt the expression the comment documents — and it still compiles, because it is only a comment. Fixed by describing the clause in prose.
plan.risks:
1. WHAT I CONCEDE. The gating objection was correct and I did not do the step-zero search before writing SQL. The estate names these builders in its landmine corpus precisely so this does not happen, and I read that corpus for a different entry the same afternoon without asking whether it named a helper for the predicate I was about to write.

2. WHAT I DO NOT CONCEDE, AND WHY IT IS NOT DEFENSIVENESS. This check must NOT adopt PageHasShippedPredicateFor as its ~14 siblings do. That predicate excludes every never-shipped page; bugs_open/093 put the content_data surface into this scan specifically to catch copy BEFORE it publishes. Adopting the sibling convention wholesale would silence the check on exactly the pre-publication copy it exists to read. The divergence is now documented at the call site with its reason, which is the form the estate already uses at resolve_internal_links_action.go:575.

3. SHARED SEAM, CONSUMERS NAMED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). Unchanged from round 1: two live consumers, the emit side (UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run, check_unverified_claims.go:86, fleet-wide on the discovery rotation) and the review-queue revalidator (revalidate_unverified_claims.go:199), and they change together by design — that is what the predicate-parity doc comment is for. No third consumer; other references are tests. Round 2 adds a THIRD party to name: datahelpers.NeverDeployedPagePredicateFor is now a dependency of this query, so a change to that builder changes what this scanner covers. That is the intended direction (one definition, one place to change it) but it is a new coupling and should be stated, not discovered.

4. STILL DOES NOT RETIRE a355d78b. An excluded page yields no scan row, so the arm becomes page_absent — a refusal, not a closure. Deliberately left open so the first sweep after the roll shows scan_still_trips -> page_absent, which is the only live proof the exclusion fired. Cancelling it first would destroy that evidence.

5. ARCHITECTURE SCOPE — ANSWERED BY THE SEAT, NOT BY ME. Round 1's architecture seat returned point_fix and approved: no new namespace, dedupe key, delivery guarantee, schema column or exported cross-package symbol; the emit side and revalidator already form one coupled unit. The guardian seat approved conditionally on no prior ruling making this WHERE clause a protected contract; none surfaced. I raised the question rather than deciding it and consider it settled by those two seats unless the chair rules otherwise.

6. EDITQUALITY'S LOW POINT, ACCEPTED. Several edits here are comment-only and should not count toward substantive coverage. Of the five listed, exactly two change executed behaviour (the predicate, and the test); the rest are disclosure, correction and gofmt compliance.

7. STILL INERT UNTIL A FLEET ROLL. Go changes need a rebuild; releases are whole-fleet and not this lane's to run. The 2026-08-16 sweep will run the old binary and a355d78b will still read scan_still_trips — expected, not a failure.
